summary: MEASURED allocator defect, two parts. (1) The size rounding ((n==0?1:n)+align-1)/align*align OVERFLOWS: n=SIZE_MAX-5, align=64 rounds to 0, and aligned_alloc(64,0) returns a NON-NULL pointer on glibc - so operator new hands back a 64-byte block for an ~18-exabyte request instead of throwing bad_alloc, and the caller writes far past it. (2) The four nothrow forms call tally_and_alloc directly rather than alloc_or_throw, so an installed new_handler never runs for new(std::nothrow) - a deviation from [new.delete.single]. E6 because the TU is Linux-only, b_sanitize=none-only, build_tests=true-only, in no shipped artifact, and neither it nor libyuzu_agent_core.so makes an over-aligned allocation of that size. Reporter notes its brief's instinct was BLOCKING but the derived band LOW governs, and it is explicitly NOT a policy floor (the floor list enumerates leak/double-free/UAF/borrowed-data-escape/unjoined-thread/shell-construction/undocumented-cast; an undersized-return-on-overflow is none). Fix: guard n > SIZE_MAX - align, and route the nothrow forms through a try/catch on alloc_or_throw. NOTE the structural reason this survived: the one file in the repo holding raw malloc/aligned_alloc/free is the one file no sanitizer will ever see.
